internal-review-repo. The model stays Claude Code claude-sonnet-5-5. Only the workers change (prompt, assets, skills,
the agent's own settings, effort, max_context_fraction); the positions' function text, contracts and everything else
of rw_313df9cf84a4 stay as they are.

made from reading the manuscripts [J2–J5], the same judge line moved the same 15 manuscripts by up to 6 rubric points
between two readings, three times the kept margin [J6], the content items sat at the ceiling and moved together [J6],
and N3b's put-back was never run [A2]. This round decides between **cand-g2** (incumbent, tuner release/… at 1e2f008)
and **cand-h4** (tuner release/candidates/cand-h4 at 94b91bb) with judging that can tell them apart, and runs the
put-back the objective names. No new diagnosis and no new candidate.

two workers changed, `"resources": []`, budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds, worker.image
sha256:1c386c95…, and the environment images N3b names. Held-out: paper_45 (rw_5c4743418b6b), paper_32 (rw_686e5b0bd6da) and paper_17 (rw_e263f2a52297),
which no round has read, each at checkpoint c0 in the state root issue-396-heldout with the environment image its
world records (sha256:1a1fe2c82ea277a5b0b7fac33ac2001c67dfd15bb1c57ca5dd15cbfa5722d60a, sha256:7ef042b9fda6f1e98bc0a81d64b93edf36d8dbd229b17d5e88116b0a25db882f and sha256:7a8b1bb91072c88ae18adafdead9d2198d53b823dfaf3f54d1e20ac107632b84). 5 runs of each worker per paper, all made in this world. A run whose
world ends without a release is a **failed run**: it is reported, counted in the release rate, and given the worst
score on every measure; it is never judged from a draft [D5].

**What is measured** [D3]. The decisive measure is the **number of verified content defects** in a manuscript (lower is
better), because it does not saturate the way rubric v2's 0–4 content items did (28 of 45 held-out results at 20/20):

- a defect is a claim the writing material does not support, a claim stated stronger than the evidence allows, a
  figure or table read wrongly, or a citation placed where it supports nothing;
- each defect is written as a verbatim quotation from the manuscript with its page, the material (file and location)
  that shows it is a defect, and its kind;
- a defect counts only when its quotation is found in that manuscript (C2, or the same check run by the task-setter
  before the label table is published) and its material location exists.

Rubric v2 (sha256 5df317ee…f1250) is still scored on every manuscript and reported item by item for continuity; it
decides nothing. The verifier is reported for every manuscript as a sanity floor and decides nothing.

**How the judging is made trustworthy.**

- **Reading.** The judge reads each manuscript in full, one at a time: at most 3 results per judging turn, each
  printed whole before its judgement is written, and the judgement pushed before the next is opened [D2]. A judgement
  set whose quotations C2 does not find is sent back, not counted.
- **Nothing that tells the worker.** The judge receives, per label, the manuscript and its source only. The verifier
  output (pages, citation coverage) is withheld from the judge until every judgement is pushed, and the objective's
  account of how workers differ goes to the diagnostician and the tuner, not to the judge [D7, J9].
- **Duplicates.** For each paper the task-setter re-labels 2 results of each worker as new labels, mixed into the
  same set, so that the judge reads 12 results twice without knowing it [D3]. The **drift** is the mean absolute
  difference between the two judgements of a duplicate, in defect count.
- **Calibration.** Per paper, one known-worse draft (a held-out manuscript with three unsupported claims and one misread
  figure inserted; the task-setter keeps the key) goes into the blind set under an ordinary label [D6]. Calibration
  passes only if that judgement quotes at least 3 of the 4 inserted defects; if it fails on any paper, the judging is
  fixed and every judgement of that paper is redone before any comparison.
- **One reading.** All results of all papers are judged in the same judging pass, interleaved across workers and
  papers in label order; a change of judge line restarts the pass. One judge line: Codex gpt-6.1-sol, effort high, through HuTian's own Codex login,
  no fallback.

**How candidates are told apart** [D4]. For each paper, take each worker's mean defect count over its 5 runs (failed
runs included as stated above). The difference is the mean over papers of (cand-h4 mean − cand-g2 mean). Its standard
error comes from the within-paper spread of the runs, unpaired (runs are independent; rep numbers pair nothing):
SE = √(Σ_papers (s²_h4/5 + s²_g2/5)) / n_papers. cand-h4 is kept only if all of these hold:

1. its defect count is lower by more than 2 SE **and** by more than the measured drift;
2. its release rate is not lower than cand-g2's by more than 1 run in 15;
3. its rubric v2 form items (page budget, template, sections) are not lower by more than 1 SE.

SE, the drift, the calibration result, the release rates, and the rubric v2 items. With 5 runs per paper the SE of N3's
totals was about 0.9 rubric points [J7]; if the drift exceeds the observed difference, say that the round could not
tell the workers apart rather than keeping either.

sha256:731fc3cf… (paper_29). It counts only if that world was made by this round and its records show the kept worker
producing new output. No position may substitute another world: if the named world cannot run, the round ends
unresolved and says why.

- judge: judgements from reading, with quotations; no approval while its own record lists a requirement as pending, and
  none on a round made by an earlier world [A2, D1, D2];
- task-setter: every world made from a held-out start is in the run records or listed as excluded with a reason [D8];
  the blind package holds no verifier output; duplicates and calibration drafts are hidden among the labels;
- coach: problems.md is brought up to date at the round's start (N3b kept N3's stale P1) [D10]; the objective is not
  changed by any position [D9].

**What stays as it is.** The target world and its positions; the model; the task settings above; the held-out and
final-test isolation; blind labels with the table's sha256 published before judging and the table after every
judgement; one judge line; the release gates of the kernel and of DojoWorld.

**Budget.** 36000 s for this world: 30 held-out runs plus 12 duplicates and 3 calibration drafts to judge (about
45 readings at one manuscript each), the put-back, and one provider stall.

issue.body:
Round N4 of improving the paper-writing worker of rw_313df9cf84a4: the workers of its positions paper-repo and
internal-review-repo. The model stays Claude Code claude-sonnet-5-5. Only the workers change (prompt, assets, skills,
the agent's own settings, effort, max_context_fraction); the positions' function text, contracts and everything else
of rw_313df9cf84a4 stay as they are.

**Why this round.** N3 and N3b kept cand-h4 over cand-g2, but that decision is not evidence: the judgements were not
made from reading the manuscripts [J2–J5], the same judge line moved the same 15 manuscripts by up to 6 rubric points
between two readings, three times the kept margin [J6], the content items sat at the ceiling and moved together [J6],
and N3b's put-back was never run [A2]. This round decides between **cand-g2** (incumbent, tuner release/… at 1e2f008)
and **cand-h4** (tuner release/candidates/cand-h4 at 94b91bb) with judging that can tell them apart, and runs the
put-back the objective names. No new diagnosis and no new candidate.

**Tasks.** As in N3: each task is one paper, written in a world continued from that paper's world at c0, with only the
two workers changed, `"resources": []`, budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds, worker.image
sha256:1c386c95…, and the environment images N3b names. Held-out: paper_45 (rw_5c4743418b6b), paper_32 (rw_686e5b0bd6da) and paper_17 (rw_e263f2a52297),
which no round has read, each at checkpoint c0 in the state root issue-396-heldout with the environment image its
world records (sha256:1a1fe2c82ea277a5b0b7fac33ac2001c67dfd15bb1c57ca5dd15cbfa5722d60a, sha256:7ef042b9fda6f1e98bc0a81d64b93edf36d8dbd229b17d5e88116b0a25db882f and sha256:7a8b1bb91072c88ae18adafdead9d2198d53b823dfaf3f54d1e20ac107632b84). 5 runs of each worker per paper, all made in this world. A run whose
world ends without a release is a **failed run**: it is reported, counted in the release rate, and given the worst
score on every measure; it is never judged from a draft [D5].

**What is measured** [D3]. The decisive measure is the **number of verified content defects** in a manuscript (lower is
better), because it does not saturate the way rubric v2's 0–4 content items did (28 of 45 held-out results at 20/20):

- a defect is a claim the writing material does not support, a claim stated stronger than the evidence allows, a
  figure or table read wrongly, or a citation placed where it supports nothing;
- each defect is written as a verbatim quotation from the manuscript with its page, the material (file and location)
  that shows it is a defect, and its kind;
- a defect counts only when its quotation is found in that manuscript (C2, or the same check run by the task-setter
  before the label table is published) and its material location exists.

Rubric v2 (sha256 5df317ee…f1250) is still scored on every manuscript and reported item by item for continuity; it
decides nothing. The verifier is reported for every manuscript as a sanity floor and decides nothing.

**How the judging is made trustworthy.**

- **Reading.** The judge reads each manuscript in full, one at a time: at most 3 results per judging turn, each
  printed whole before its judgement is written, and the judgement pushed before the next is opened [D2]. A judgement
  set whose quotations C2 does not find is sent back, not counted.
- **Nothing that tells the worker.** The judge receives, per label, the manuscript and its source only. The verifier
  output (pages, citation coverage) is withheld from the judge until every judgement is pushed, and the objective's
  account of how workers differ goes to the diagnostician and the tuner, not to the judge [D7, J9].
- **Duplicates.** For each paper the task-setter re-labels 2 results of each worker as new labels, mixed into the
  same set, so that the judge reads 12 results twice without knowing it [D3]. The **drift** is the mean absolute
  difference between the two judgements of a duplicate, in defect count.
- **Calibration.** Per paper, one known-worse draft (a held-out manuscript with three unsupported claims and one misread
  figure inserted; the task-setter keeps the key) goes into the blind set under an ordinary label [D6]. Calibration
  passes only if that judgement quotes at least 3 of the 4 inserted defects; if it fails on any paper, the judging is
  fixed and every judgement of that paper is redone before any comparison.
- **One reading.** All results of all papers are judged in the same judging pass, interleaved across workers and
  papers in label order; a change of judge line restarts the pass. One judge line: Codex gpt-6.1-sol, effort high, through HuTian's own Codex login,
  no fallback.

**How candidates are told apart** [D4]. For each paper, take each worker's mean defect count over its 5 runs (failed
runs included as stated above). The difference is the mean over papers of (cand-h4 mean − cand-g2 mean). Its standard
error comes from the within-paper spread of the runs, unpaired (runs are independent; rep numbers pair nothing):
SE = √(Σ_papers (s²_h4/5 + s²_g2/5)) / n_papers. cand-h4 is kept only if all of these hold:

1. its defect count is lower by more than 2 SE **and** by more than the measured drift;
2. its release rate is not lower than cand-g2's by more than 1 run in 15;
3. its rubric v2 form items (page budget, template, sections) are not lower by more than 1 SE.

Otherwise cand-g2 stays. Report every number: per-run defect counts, per-paper means and spreads, the difference, its
SE, the drift, the calibration result, the release rates, and the rubric v2 items. With 5 runs per paper the SE of N3's
totals was about 0.9 rubric points [J7]; if the drift exceeds the observed difference, say that the round could not
tell the workers apart rather than keeping either.

**Put-back** [A2, D9]. Put the kept worker back into rw_313df9cf84a4 at c0 with worker.environment_image
sha256:731fc3cf… (paper_29). It counts only if that world was made by this round and its records show the kept worker
producing new output. No position may substitute another world: if the named world cannot run, the round ends
unresolved and says why.

**Positions' work this round asks for** (the problems that were workers' in N3/N3b):

- judge: judgements from reading, with quotations; no approval while its own record lists a requirement as pending, and
  none on a round made by an earlier world [A2, D1, D2];
- task-setter: every world made from a held-out start is in the run records or listed as excluded with a reason [D8];
  the blind package holds no verifier output; duplicates and calibration drafts are hidden among the labels;
- coach: problems.md is brought up to date at the round's start (N3b kept N3's stale P1) [D10]; the objective is not
  changed by any position [D9].

**What stays as it is.** The target world and its positions; the model; the task settings above; the held-out and
final-test isolation; blind labels with the table's sha256 published before judging and the table after every
judgement; one judge line; the release gates of the kernel and of DojoWorld.

**Budget.** 36000 s for this world: 30 held-out runs plus 12 duplicates and 3 calibration drafts to judge (about
45 readings at one manuscript each), the put-back, and one provider stall.
